The common-law Rule Against Perpetuities, applied as of the 1960 conveyance, voids the shifting executory interest in the sister’s children who reach 25, because a child born late in her life can turn 25 more than 21 years after every person then alive has died, and church use can first occur even later. Striking that interest leaves the friend with a fee simple absolute; later births and deaths do not restore it. Title is in the friend only (A).

CONFIDENCE: 86
